mainTopic: Nullifying the vows of a betrothed young woman (נערה המאורסה) who was divorced and betrothed again on the same day: her father together with her last ארוס can nullify, even vows made while she was betrothed to the first ארוס.
overview: The משנה teaches a case about a betrothed נערה who made a vow, was divorced, and was betrothed again on the same day, even many times. In that case her father and her last ארוס together nullify her vows. The rule is that as long as she was never independent for even one moment, her father and her latest ארוס share the power of הפרה. The גמרא asks for the source that a later ארוס can nullify vows that came under the first ארוס. שמואל learns it from the פסוק "וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ", meaning vows already on her. When the גמרא suggests this might cover only vows the first ארוס never had, it answers that the extra word "עָלֶיהָ" includes them too. A ברייתא supports שמואל, and it adds that if the ארוס nullified and died before the father heard, the father can nullify the husband's share. רבי נתן says that last ruling is only the view of בית שמאי, while בית הלל say the father cannot nullify alone. The גמרא then asks what the two schools are really arguing about, and the answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Betrothed again on the same day: father and last husband nullify
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a betrothed נערה who vowed, was divorced, and was betrothed again that same day (even a hundred times) has her vows nullified by her father and her last ארוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a girl made a vow while she was betrothed, then was divorced that same day and betrothed to someone else that same day, even a hundred times over, her father and her last husband nullify her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case: a betrothed girl vows, gets divorced, and gets betrothed again on the same day. It rules that her father and her newest ארוס can nullify the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a betrothed נערה's vows are nullified by her father and her ארוס together. The משנה adds something new: even after a divorce and a new betrothal, the new ארוס steps in and joins the father. This works as long as it all happens on the same day, which is the day of hearing for הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)

phrases.english: MISHNA: She made a vow while she was betrothed.
She was divorced on that same day,
and she was betrothed again on that same day,
even to a hundred men, one after another,
her father and her last husband
nullify her vows.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A betrothed נערה who vowed and was then divorced and re-betrothed on the same day has her vows nullified by her father together with her last ארוס.

steps.title: The general rule: never independent for a moment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the principle: as long as the girl never entered her own authority for even one moment, her father and last husband nullify her vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: any girl who did not leave into her own authority for even one moment has her vows nullified by her father and her last husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the case with one general rule that explains when the father and the latest husband share the power to nullify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point is whether there was ever a break in the father's authority. If she never became fully independent, even for one moment, the chain stays connected. The father plus whoever is her current ארוס can then nullify.

keyTerms.meaning: Her own authority (independent, not under father or husband)

steps.whatToRemember: The power of father plus latest ארוס stays alive as long as the girl was never independent, even for a moment.

phrases.english: This is the rule: any girl who did not
go out into her own authority for even one moment,
phrases.notes: This means she was never on her own, for example through full marriage or growing up past נערה age.

phrases.english: her father and her last husband nullify her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Generalizes the case of step 1 into a principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whenever the girl never entered her own authority even briefly, her father and her latest husband nullify her vows.

steps.title: Source for the last ארוס nullifying the first one's vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a later ארוס can nullify vows that already came under the first ארוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know that the last betrothed man can nullify vows that were seen by the first betrothed man?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from. How can a new ארוס cancel vows that were made back when she belonged to a different ארוס?
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think each ארוס only deals with vows made during his own betrothal. The משנה says the new ארוס can handle vows from the earlier period too. The גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A betrothed man (the husband after קידושין)
That were "seen" by, meaning they came under his zone

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we know that the last betrothed man
can nullify vows that were seen
phrases.notes: Literally "seen": the vows were made while she was betrothed to the first man, so they already fell under him.

phrases.english: by the first betrothed man?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן דְּאָרוּס אַחֲרוֹן מֵיפֵר נְדָרִים שֶׁנִּרְאוּ לְאָרוּס רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the scriptural source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source showing that a later ארוס can nullify vows that already came under an earlier ארוס.

steps.title: שמואל: "her vows upon her" means vows already on her
steps.stepSummary: שמואל derives the rule from the פסוק "וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ", meaning vows that were already on her before this husband came along.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The פסוק says "And if she shall be to a man, and her vows are upon her". This means vows that were already upon her.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question with a פסוק. It describes a husband dealing with vows that were already on the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about a woman who "becomes" someone's wife while her vows are "upon her". So the new husband can nullify vows that existed before he arrived. That covers vows from the time of an earlier ארוס.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, a sage of the גמרא

phrases.english: שמואל said: The verse states:
"And if she shall be to a man
and her vows are upon her".
This means vows that were already upon her.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "וּנְדָרֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ" refers to vows already upon her, so the new husband can nullify vows from before his betrothal.

steps.title: Maybe only vows the first ארוס never had
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's proof: maybe the פסוק covers only vows the first ארוס had no link to, but not vows that came under him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps this applies only to vows that were not seen by the first betrothed man. But vows that were seen by the first betrothed, the last betrothed cannot nullify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל. The פסוק may only show that a husband can cancel earlier vows in general, such as vows from before any betrothal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between vows that were made before any husband was involved and vows that already belonged to the first ארוס. The פסוק could be teaching only the first kind. If so, it does not prove the משנה's case, where the vows were made under the first ארוס.

phrases.english: Perhaps these words apply only
to vows that were not seen by the first betrothed,
but vows that were seen by the first betrothed,
the last betrothed cannot nullify!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי שֶׁלֹּא נִרְאוּ לְאָרוּס רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether שמואל's פסוק actually proves the משנה's case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק may only cover vows with no prior ארוס, not vows that already came under a first ארוס, so it does not prove the משנה.

steps.title: "Upon her" is an extra word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word "עָלֶיהָ" is extra in the פסוק, so it comes to include even vows that came under the first ארוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word "upon her" is an extra word in the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. The word "עָלֶיהָ" was not needed for the basic meaning, so it is there to teach something more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תורה uses an extra word, the גמרא reads it as adding a new case. Here the extra "עָלֶיהָ" stretches the rule to cover every vow already on her. That includes vows that were under the first ארוס, so the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra, unneeded word in the פסוק that teaches something new

steps.whatToRemember: The extra word "עָלֶיהָ" teaches that the last ארוס can nullify even vows that were under an earlier ארוס.

phrases.english: "Upon her" is an extra word in the verse.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word (ייתור) widens the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only covers vows never under a prior ארוס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra "עָלֶיהָ" includes all vows already on her, even those under the first ארוס.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting שמואל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports שמואל: if the father nullified and the ארוס died before hearing, then even after a new betrothal that day, the father and last husband nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like שמואל: For a betrothed young girl, her father and husband nullify her vows. How? If her father heard and nullified for her, and the husband did not manage to hear before he died, and she was betrothed that same day, even a hundred times, her father and last husband nullify her vows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches שמואל's view. In its case, the vow was made under the first ארוס, and the later ארוס still nullifies it together with the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow in the ברייתא was made while she was betrothed to the first man. It was "seen" by him, but he died before he heard it. Since the last ארוס can still join the father to nullify, this is exactly שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with his view
Did not manage (did not have time)

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא like שמואל:
A betrothed young girl:
her father and her husband nullify her vows. How so?
If her father heard and nullified for her,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק הַבַּעַל לִשְׁמוֹעַ עַד שֶׁמֵּת,
phrases.english: and the husband did not manage to hear before he died,
and she was betrothed on that same day,
and even a hundred times,
her father and her last husband nullify her vows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא supporting שמואל's conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the last ארוס can nullify vows that came under the first ארוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that after the first ארוס died, the father and the last ארוס nullify

steps.title: Husband nullified and died: father nullifies the husband's share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the husband nullified and died before the father heard, the father can still nullify the husband's share.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her husband heard and nullified for her, and the father did not manage to hear before the husband died, the father goes back and nullifies the husband's share.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds the opposite case. Here the husband nullified first and then died before the father heard, and it rules that the father can still finish the nullification.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothed girl's vow needs both the father and the ארוס to nullify. According to this ברייתא, when the ארוס dies after nullifying, his part does not just disappear. The father takes over the husband's share and can nullify it. The next step shows that not everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband's share (his part in the nullification)

steps.whatToRemember: With a betrothed נערה, father and ארוס share the power of הפרה. If the ארוס dies, a new ארוס can take his place. This ברייתא also says the father can take over the husband's share, but the next step shows that רבי נתן says only בית שמאי hold this.

phrases.english: If her husband heard and nullified for her,
and the father did not manage to hear
before the husband died,

phrases.aramaic: חוֹזֵר הָאָב וּמֵפֵר חֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל.
phrases.english: the father goes back and nullifies the husband's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the reverse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the ארוס nullified and died before the father heard, the father can nullify the husband's share.

steps.title: רבי נתן: This ruling is only the view of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the ברייתא's ruling, that the father nullifies alone after the ארוס died, follows בית שמאי. בית הלל say the father cannot nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: This is the view of בית שמאי. But בית הלל say the father cannot nullify.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן tells us that the ruling we just learned in the ברייתא is not everyone's opinion. It is the view of בית שמאי, and בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, the ברייתא said the father can still nullify the husband's share after the ארוס died. רבי נתן says only בית שמאי hold this. בית הלל say the father cannot nullify the vow on his own, so the vow stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who explains which school the ברייתא follows
The school of הלל, whose rulings we usually follow

steps.confusionAlert: בית הלל are not saying the vow can never be nullified. They are saying the father cannot nullify it alone once the ארוס is gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since we usually follow בית הלל, this changes how far the ברייתא's ruling can be relied on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said:
These are the words of Beit Shammai.
phrases.notes: He means the ruling we just learned in step 8, that the father can still nullify the husband's share after the ארוס died.

phrases.english: But Beit Hillel say:
He cannot nullify.
phrases.notes: "He" is the father. He cannot nullify the vow on his own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: הֵן הֵן דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the ברייתא's ruling in step 8 as the view of בית שמאי and brings the opposing view of בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the father can nullify alone after the ארוס died. According to בית הלל, he cannot.

steps.title: What are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the underlying reason is for the disagreement between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל. This is a setup line that prepares the answer coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know the two opinions, but not the reasoning behind them. The גמרא wants to find the core principle that splits the two schools.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root of an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions just brought by רבי נתן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that causes בית שמאי and בית הלל to disagree about whether the father can nullify alone.
